A narrow, written exemption 1 Put it in the statute. Assurances and FAQs can't override the text. An exemption needs to be in the Act or Rules. 2 Purpose, not status. Cover journalistic activity in the public interest, including freelancers, not just registered media houses. 3 Keep the core duties. Security safeguards and breach notice should still apply. Newsrooms hold sensitive data too. 4 Shield sources. s. 36 demands on journalistic material should need independent or judicial approval. 5 Balance erasure. A public-interest test before published reports or archives must be removed. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 06 / 08

TA K E AWAY Privacy and a free press both protect the citizen. People need protection from careless or malicious use of their data, and the public needs journalism that can investigate the powerful. The answer is a narrow, conditional exemption written into the law, not no exemption and not a blanket one. Adv.
